title: What If the Whole World Used One Time Zone?

scenes.text: What if the whole planet ran on one clock? Your noon could be someone else's midnight.
It already happens in China. One clock spans a country as wide as the continental United States.
In far western China, the sun can rise around ten in the morning in winter on the official clock.
Summer sunsets there come near eleven at night. Many locals keep an unofficial clock two hours behind.
Spain shows the cost. Its clock runs almost two hours ahead of the sun in places, and bedtimes slide later.
So one world clock would be easy for flights and calls, but half the planet would eat lunch in the dark.

description:
What if the whole world used one time zone?
China already does it across a country as wide as the continental US, and the sun rises as late as ten in the morning on the clock in the far west.
